examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform Using Partial Fractions
examples.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\dfrac{3s}{(s-4)(s+2)}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\dfrac{3s}{(s-4)(s+2)} = \dfrac{2}{s-4} + \dfrac{1}{s+2}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{4t}} & =\frac{1}{s-4},\,s>4, \\ L{{e}^{-2t}} & =\frac{1}{s+2},\,s>-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{s-4}+\frac{1}{s+2}} & =2{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-4}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+2}} \\  & =2{e}^{4t}+{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\dfrac{3s}{(s-4)(s+2)}$ is

$$
\mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ F(s) \right\} = f(t)=2e^{4t} + e^{-2t}.
$$

feedback.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{4}{{s}^{3}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{2}} & =\frac{2!}{{s}^{2+1}}=\frac{2}{{s}^{3}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{2}} & =\frac{2}{{s}^{3}} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{t}^{2}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{3}}} \\ {t}^{2} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{3}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{3}}} & ={t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{3}}}={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{{s}^{3}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{{s}^{3}}}=2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
